title: Cryoport Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

- *Third quarter revenue grew 14% year-over-year to $50.2 million*
- *Commercial Cell and Gene Therapy revenue increased 20% year-over-year*
- *Supporting a record 788 global clinical trials and 23 commercially approved cell and gene therapies as of September 30, 2026*
- *Raises full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $197 million - $199 million*


NASHVILLE, Tenn.


, Nov. 5, 2026


/PRNewswire/ --[Cryoport, Inc.](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4815747-1&h=2164701350&u=https%3A%2F%2Fcryoportinc.com%2F&a=Cryoport%2C+Inc.) (NASDAQ: CYRX) ("Cryoport" or the "Company"), a leading global provider of integrated temperature-controlled supply chain solutions for the life sciences, today announced financial results for its third quarter (Q3) and first nine months (9M) of 2026.


Jerrell Shelton, CEO of Cryoport, stated, "Cryoport delivered third quarter revenue of $50.2 million, reflecting continued momentum across our core cell and gene therapy (CGT) business. Revenue from commercial CGT clients increased 20% year over year, BioStorage/BioServices revenue expanded 25%, and total Life Sciences Services revenue grew 18%, underscoring the strength of our integrated platform and the growing demand for our solutions. These results reflect both the increasing number of patients worldwide receiving CGT treatments and the continued adoption of our end-to-end temperature-controlled supply chain solutions. We also achieved 8% year over year growth in Life Sciences Products revenue, supported by MVE Biological Solutions' (MVE) position as the global market leader in cryogenic systems.


"During the quarter, we further strengthened our leadership position within the CGT ecosystem, ending the period supporting 23 commercial therapies and a record of 788 clinical trials worldwide. Our integrated platform, disciplined execution, and growing utilization of our Global Supply Chain Center Network continue to enhance scalability and operating leverage, advancing our progress toward sustained profitability. This momentum was reflected in our positive adjusted EBITDA of $1.1 million for the quarter, representing another important milestone in our pathway to profitability initiative.


"Our strong year-to-date performance, combined with expanding support of commercial therapies, deepening customer relationships, a robust clinical trial pipeline, and continued demand for MVE's industry-leading products, gives us confidence in our outlook. As a result, we are increasing our full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $197 million to $199 million," concluded Mr. Shelton.

BioLogistics Solutions revenue increased 16% year-over-year in Q3 2026, driven by continued commercial therapies development, and clinical trial progress within the CGT market. BioStorage/BioServices revenue grew 25% year-over-year, reflecting another strong quarter of demand for our expanded, integrated services offering, which provides seamless, secure handling of temperature-sensitive materials across our global network.


As of September 30, 2026, the number of commercial cell and gene therapies we support increased to 23 and our total global clinical trial count that we support rose to 788 clinical trials, a net increase of 43 clinical trials over September 30, 2025, with 99 of these clinical trials in Phase 3. In Q3 2026, Cryoport's customer, Replimune, received accelerated U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for TUDRIQEV™ for the treatment of adults with unresectable advanced cutaneous melanoma, a skin cancer that has spread too widely or deeply to be safely or completely removed with surgery. Also, during the quarter Crispr Therapeutics and their partner Vertex Pharmaceuticals received FDA supplemental approval to expand the label of CASGEVY® for treatment of people 2 years of age and older with either Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) or Transfusion-dependent Beta Thalassemia (TDT). CASGEVY is the first approved genetic therapy indicated for children as young as 2 years for both SCD and TDT .


Two of Cryoport's customers filed Biologics License Applications (BLA) with the FDA in the third quarter and we anticipate another five possible BLA or Marketing Authorization Applications (MAA) in 2026. Cryoport also anticipates two possible additional new therapy approvals (both of which have received Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) dates from the FDA for Q4 2026), and one possible additional supplemental approval for geographic expansion from our customer base this year.


**Operational Milestones**


- *Cryoport Systems initiated BioLogistics services at its new state-of-the-art Global Supply Chain Center located in Santa Ana, California.*
- *Cryoport Systems' Global Supply Chain Center in Paris, France, received ISO 9001 and ISO 21973 certifications. ISO 21973 certification is the first international standard developed specifically to address the transportation risks associated with human cells for therapeutic use.*
- *CRYOGENE secured new BioStorage and service contracts with customers including Houston Methodist Medical Center, Sonic Clinical Trials, and XenoSTART.*


**Financial Highlights**


On June 11, 2025, the Company completed the divestiture of its CRYOPDP specialty courier business to DHL Group. The results of CRYOPDP, a former business within Cryoport's Life Sciences Services segment, are presented as discontinued operations for all periods and are excluded from the non-GAAP financial measures in this release.


**Revenue**


- *Total revenue for Q3 2026 was $50.2 million, compared to $44.2 million for Q3 2025, a year-over-year increase of 14%, or $6.0 million.*


- *Life Sciences Services revenue for Q3 2026 (representing 57% of our total revenue) was $28.6 million, compared to $24.3 million for Q3 2025, up 18% year-over-year, including BioStorage/BioServices revenue of $6.0 million, up 25% year-over-year.*
- *Life Sciences Products revenue for Q3 2026 (representing 43% of our total revenue) was $21.7 million, compared to $20.0 million for Q3 2025.*


- *Total revenue for* *9M 2026* *was $147.0 million, compared to $130.7 million for 9M 2025.*


- *Life Sciences Services revenue for 9M 2026 was $83.4 million, compared to $71.5 million for 9M 2025, including BioStorage/BioServices revenue of $16.9 million, compared to $13.7 million for 9M 2025.*
- *Life Sciences Products revenue for 9M 2026 was $63.6 million, compared to $59.2 million for 9M 2025.*


**Gross Margin**


- *Total gross margin was 47.5% for Q3 2026, compared to 48.2% for Q3 2025.*


- *Gross margin for Life Sciences Services was 50.4% for Q3 2026, compared to 49.7% for Q3 2025.*
- *Gross margin for Life Sciences Products was 43.6% for Q3 2026, compared to 46.4% for Q3 2025.*


- *Total gross margin* *was 46.7% for 9M 2026, compared to 46.9% for 9M 2025.*


- *Gross margin for Life Sciences Services was 49.7% for 9M 2026, compared to 48.8% for 9M 2025.*
- *Gross margin for Life Sciences Products was 42.6% for 9M 2026, compared to 44.6% for 9M 2025.*


**Operating Costs and Expenses**


- *Operating costs and expenses were $32.6 million for Q3 2026, compared to $31.3 million for Q3 2025. Operating costs and expenses were $97.0 million for 9M 2026, compared to $88.1 million for 9M 2025.*


**Loss from Continuing Operations**


- *Loss from continuing operations was $10.9 million for Q3 2026, compared to a loss of $6.7 million for Q3 2025. Loss from continuing operations was $28.5 million for 9M 2026, compared to a loss of $25.4 million for 9M 2025.*


**Net Income (Loss) – including Discontinued Operations**


- *Net loss was $10.9 million for Q3 2026, compared to net loss of $6.9 million for Q3 2025. Net loss for 9M 2026 was $29.7 million, compared to net income of $89.9 million for 9M 2025. Net income for 9M 2025 was primarily driven by the sale of our CRYOPDP specialty courier business during Q2 2025, which contributed $115.4 million, net of taxes, to income from discontinued operations.*
- *Net loss attributable to common stockholders for Q3 2026 was $12.9 million, or $0.25 per share. Net loss attributable to common stockholders for 9M 2026 was $35.7 million, or $0.71 per share. This compares to net loss attributable to common stockholders of $8.9 million, or $0.18 per share, and net income attributable to common stockholders of $83.9 million, or $1.68 per share, for Q3 2025 and 9M 2025, respectively.*


**Adjusted EBITDA from Continuing Operations**


- *Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations was $1.1 million for Q3 2026, compared to a negative $0.6 million for Q3 2025. Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations for 9M 2026 was $0.9 million, compared to a negative $4.4 million for 9M 2025.*


**Cash, Cash equivalents, and Short-Term Investments**


- *Cryoport held $393.1 million in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments as of September 30, 2026.*


**Revenue Guidance for Full-Year 2026**


- *The Company is providing updated full-year 2026 revenue guidance in the range of $197 million to $199 million. The Company's 2026 revenue guidance is dependent on its current business and expectations, which may be impacted by, among other things, factors that are outside of our control, such as national economic factors, the global macroeconomic and geopolitical environment, supply chain constraints, inflationary pressures, tariffs and other trade restrictions and/or the effects of foreign currency fluctuations, as well as the other factors described in the Company's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"), including in the "Risk Factors" section of its most recently filed periodic reports on Form 10-K and Form 10-Q, as well as in its subsequent filings with the SEC.*

**About Cryoport, Inc.**


[Cryoport, Inc.](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4815747-1&h=3206682616&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.cryoportinc.com%2F&a=Cryoport%2C+Inc.) (Nasdaq: CYRX) is a leading global provider of integrated temperature-controlled supply chain solutions for the life sciences, with an emphasis on regenerative medicine. We support biopharmaceutical companies, contract manufacturers (CDMOs), contract research organizations (CROs), developers, and researchers with a comprehensive suite of services and products designed to minimize risk and maximize reliability across the temperature-controlled supply chain for the life sciences. Our integrated supply chain platform includes the Cryoportal® Logistics Management Platform, advanced temperature-controlled packaging, informatics, specialized BioLogistics, BioStorage, BioServices, cryopreservation services, and cryogenic systems, which in varying combinations deliver end-to-end solutions that meet the rigorous demands of the life sciences. With innovation, regulatory compliance, and agility at our core, we are ***"Enabling the Future of Medicine™* *."***


Headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee, our company maintains a strong global presence with operations across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC.

**Note Regarding Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


To supplement our financial statements, which are presented on the basis of U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP), the following non-GAAP measure of financial performance as defined in Regulation G of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 is included in this release: adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations. Non-GAAP financial measures are not calculated in accordance with GAAP, are not based on any comprehensive set of accounting rules or principles and may be different from non-GAAP financial measures presented by other companies. Non-GAAP financial measures, including adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations, should not be considered as a substitute for, or superior to, measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP.


Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations is defined as loss from continuing operations adjusted for net interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization expense, stock-based compensation expense, acquisition and integration costs, cost reduction initiatives, investment income, unrealized (gain)/loss on investments, foreign currency loss, changes in fair value of contingent consideration and charges or gains resulting from non-recurring events, as applicable.


Management believes that adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations provides a useful measure of Cryoport's operating results, a meaningful comparison with historical results and with the results of other companies, and insight into Cryoport's ongoing operating performance. Further, management and the Company's board of directors utilize adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations to gain a better understanding of Cryoport's comparative operating performance from period to period and as a basis for planning and forecasting future periods. Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations is also a significant performance measure used by Cryoport in connection with its incentive compensation programs. Management believes adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations, when read in conjunction with Cryoport's GAAP financials, is useful to investors because it provides a basis for meaningful period-to-period comparisons of Cryoport's ongoing operating results, including results of operations, against investor and analyst financial models, helps identify trends in Cryoport's underlying business and in performing related trend analyses, and it provides a better understanding of how management plans and measures Cryoport's underlying business.
